Detailed method

A lid sits on this tin loaf. Currently 500 g flour, 66% hydration, 2% salt, and 1% yeast. That is 330 g water, 10 g salt, and 5 g yeast, 845 g of dough. Currently 1 loaf of 845 g. Fill a straight-sided tin about halfway so the dough can rise into the lid. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 330 g water, 10 g salt, and 5 g instant yeast, then knead 8 to 10 minutes until smooth. At 66% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 1% yeast it should about double.
  3. Pan Grease a straight-sided tin and its lid. The default 845 g uses a lidded pullman pan about 33 cm long, 10 cm wide, and 10 cm high, which holds about 900 g. If you change the amount, use a pan sized to fit, or split the dough. Roll the 845 g dough into a log and set it seam-side down. It should fill the tin about halfway. This batch is 1 loaf. Oil for the tin is extra and is not in the gram total.
  4. Proof Cover the tin with the lid off for 40 to 70 minutes, until the dough rises to about 2 cm under where the lid will sit. Then slide the lid on.
  5. Bake Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Bake 25 minutes with the lid on, then 12 to 18 minutes with the lid off, until the top is golden and the sides are firm.
  6. Cool Turn it out and cool on a rack for at least 1 hour. Slice it once it is cool.
